confidence_notes: I ran six web searches: one for the RBA rate and five for prices. Beer, cappuccino and inexpensive-meal anchors come from crowdsourced cost-of-living aggregators (Numbeo-style data, MyLifeElsewhere, Traveltables, Citycost), which disagree with each other and are partly dated. Mid-range dinner for two is bounded from aggregator figures of roughly MX$970 to MX$1,500 and adjusted down to exclude drinks. I found no Querétaro-specific cocktail or restaurant wine-by-the-glass prices. Those two anchors use the usual local relationship to beer, with cocktail at about 2.8x and wine at about 2.4x, plus general Mexican restaurant pricing knowledge. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Querétaro as a mid-sized colonial and business city. I did not search for accommodation prices or inspect any listings.
comparable_city_reasoning: Querétaro is comparable to other mid-sized Mexican colonial and business cities such as Guanajuato, San Miguel de Allende and Puebla. Local aggregators put restaurant prices roughly 6% below the Mexican average and overall costs about 5% above. Its hotel rates are somewhat elevated by business travel and domestic weekend tourism.
